title: How do we draw a triangle from two angles and the side between them?
description: A base of five centimetres is drawn, an angle of forty five degrees is made at one end and eighty degrees at the other, and the two arms cross at the third corner. Keeko's doubt is that both angles can be made at the same end of the base.
teaching_notes: One idea: the side between the two given angles is the base, and each angle is made at its own end of it. Watch for students who make both angles at the same end.

source: Construct a triangle ABC where AB = 5 cm, ∠A = 45° and ∠B = 80°.
video_script.why: The child can draw a triangle from two sides and the angle between them and now draws one from two angles and the side between them.
video_script.substitution: The book's own triangle with AB five centimetres, angle A forty five degrees and angle B eighty degrees.
video_script.anchor: triangle ABC with AB five centimetres, angle A forty five degrees and angle B eighty degrees
video_script.wrong_answer: make both angles at the same end of the base
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko makes the forty five degree angle and the eighty degree angle both at A, so both arms start from the same corner and never cross anywhere new.
video_script.payoff_line: Triangle eigh bee cee is drawn with one angle at each end of the base

final_answer.spoken: triangle eigh bee cee with eigh cee about six centimetres and bee cee about four point three centimetres

maths_rules: AB = 5 cm is the side shared by both angles, the included side, and it is drawn as the base
the angle 45° is made at A and the angle 80° is made at B, on the same side of the base
the two arms cross at C, the third vertex
with the third angle 55°, AC = 5 x sin 80° / sin 55° = 6.01 cm and BC = 5 x sin 45° / sin 55° = 4.32 cm, so AC is about 6.0 cm and BC about 4.3 cm
video_script.design: One triangle is built on the board: the base first, then one arm at each end, then the crossing point. The base keeps its colour all video.
